Package com.github.crittscott.somestacks.gametest

Class ProtectionGameTests

java.lang.Object
com.github.crittscott.somestacks.gametest.ProtectionGameTests
public final class ProtectionGameTests extends Object
The rules that keep a gesture from writing where it should not: build height, entity obstruction, and native placement and interaction protection.

These fire the Forge events themselves, so they cover the order a consult and the commit that follows must agree on.

    • settleKeepsAnEmptyTopBlockWhoseRemovalIsRefused

      public static void settleKeepsAnEmptyTopBlockWhoseRemovalIsRefused(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      Forge fixture: cancel BlockEvent.BreakEvent at an empty upper Storage block above a base holding one dirt. Settlement keeps the refused block and height two; removing the veto and settling again removes the empty top.

      To check manually, grow a temporary two-block pile and configure protection to deny removal by the automation actor at the upper position while allowing extraction. Empty the upper block and allow settlement; it remains. Lift the denial and trigger another inventory change; subsequent settlement trims it.

    • blockUseDenialFreezesStackGestures

      public static void blockUseDenialFreezesStackGestures(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      Loader entry point for InteractionChecks.blockUseDenialFreezesStackGestures(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper, java.util.function.Function<net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack, net.minecraft.server.level.ServerPlayer>, com.github.crittscott.somestacks.gametest.InteractionChecks.LoaderClick, java.util.function.BiConsumer<net.minecraft.server.level.ServerPlayer, net.minecraft.core.BlockPos>, java.lang.Runnable); see that method for the scenario and manual check. The denial is a RightClickBlock listener at the default priority that sets setUseBlock(DENY) for the fixture player at the gesture's block, so it runs before the mod's own LOWEST listener, as a protection mod's would.

    • itemUseDenialLeavesStackGesturesWorking

      public static void itemUseDenialLeavesStackGesturesWorking(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      Forge permission fixture: a RightClickBlock listener at an existing Storage block denies only item use. Stack gestures are the block's own use, so a dirt deposit and an extraction both still succeed. The block-use half is blockUseDenialFreezesStackGestures(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper).

      To check manually, use a protection rule or test listener that denies item use at the stack while allowing block use: V-deposit dirt, then release V and extract it; both work.

    • nativeAdjacentDepositConsultsBothPositions

      public static void nativeAdjacentDepositConsultsBothPositions(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      Native adjacent-deposit fixture: put stone west of an empty Singles block and aim through the stone's east face toward its bottom cell. A Forge RightClickBlock listener denying block use is applied first at the clicked stone and then at the Singles destination. Either veto prevents deposit; allowing both deposits one stone.

      To check manually, put an existing Singles block east of a stone block and aim through that face while V-depositing stone. Configure protection to deny interaction at the clicked block, then only at the destination, then at neither. Only the last configuration deposits; loader-exact callback vetoes require a test listener if the protection mod lacks separate rules.

    • placementDefersNeighborPublicationAndRestoresDeniedInventory

      public static void placementDefersNeighborPublicationAndRestoresDeniedInventory(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      No in-game form: no player-visible stack placement replaces a block that holds data, so there is nothing a player could see restored. The fixture changes the facing of a named chest holding seven diamonds through the Forge edit authority's place, the capture step behind WorldEdits.placeChecked (whose gate refuses an occupied position, so it cannot drive this fixture), and its Forge EntityPlaceEvent listener alters the chest's inventory and then cancels the placement. It guards that a vetoed placement restores the prior block state and block-entity data (items and name) without notifying neighbors or emitting a game event, leaves no snapshot state behind, and that an accepted placement notifies neighbors only after the event permits it.

    • placementRefusesReentrancyAndForeignCapture

      public static void placementRefusesReentrancyAndForeignCapture(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      No in-game form: both halves need another mod acting from inside Forge's placement machinery. It guards that WorldEdits.placeChecked refuses a nested call made from inside an EntityPlaceEvent listener while the outer placement still succeeds, and that it refuses to run while another party has captureBlockSnapshots set, leaving that party's capture flag as it was.
